one_row_per: role — an opening at one employer under one title, kept forever once seen

window.rule: 2026-07-01 <= last_seen <= 2026-09-28, both inclusive (90 days) — the role was seen open on its employer's own careers board on some day in that range
window.note: ASPIRATIONAL: this store's earliest observation is 2026-08-16, which is AFTER the window start 2026-07-01. Any absence of roles before 2026-08-16 is OUR blindness, not the market's — the pipeline was not yet watching. Do not read the shape of the first days as a trend.

classifier_contract.note: rows_unknown is not a defect in the row: it is a cell stamped before the contract was recorded (2026-09-11), or a verdict served from the classifier cache without the seam reporting which contract answered. It means 'we cannot say', which is the honest reading and not 'stale'.

store.renamed_note: a role_id changes only when a card-blob title is canonicalised into the role's name; the record keeps its first_seen, episodes, emailed history and classifier verdict
store.retention: nothing is ever deleted; a wrong row becomes superseded or purged and keeps its line

excluded.note: superseded = the same posting also fetched under a second company name, kept once. purged = the COMPANY was never an employer (a registry row that points at an aggregator; a name intake rejected as an agency). withdrawn = the employer is real but THIS posting was never in scope (not in Israel, or not this employer's) — it was published in error and is listed under `removed` with its reason and the days it was public. Rows that aged out of the window are not excluded: they are in roles_archive.csv.

archive.rule: status open or closed AND last_seen < 2026-07-01 — every role the window has aged out, same columns, regenerated whole from the ledger each run

reconciliation.identity: rows + archived + superseded + purged + withdrawn + outside_window + undatable + unreadable + blocked_excluded + pending_excluded + unjudged_refused == store_records

conventions.enum_on_a_list_column: constrains each separated value, not the whole cell
conventions.empty: an empty cell means we do not hold the value, never zero and never false
conventions.encoding: UTF-8, no BOM, CRLF line endings, RFC4180 quoting

description_text.why: the full text is up to 6,000 characters per role with embedded newlines: it breaks naive parsers, and this file is committed to git every day

funnel.what: one row per full daily run: postings fetched -> Israel -> judged -> matched -> alive -> board -> emailed

role_id.doc: Opaque stable id for the role — a normalised slug derived from company_registry and title (punctuation and corporate suffixes dropped), so DO NOT split it: use the company_registry and title columns. It is the join key for roles_text.jsonl.

company.doc: The employer's brand name where company-intel evidenced one (the same rule the board renders by), else the registry name. Group by this.

company_registry.doc: The registry/record name — the stable join key to this repo's other files (firmographics, the ledger); role_id derives from it. Equal to company when no brand is evidenced.

location.doc: Location as posted (free text, usually an Israeli city).

url.doc: The posting's own address on the employer's careers board.

status.doc: open = still on the employer's board at last_seen; closed = it was gone when we last looked.

enum.open: still listed on the employer's own careers board when we last looked
enum.closed: we looked at that board again and the posting was gone

posted_date.doc: The date the EMPLOYER states the role was posted. Empty when the board publishes none.

first_seen.doc: The first day this pipeline ever saw the role, across all of its spells. Not a posting date.

last_seen.doc: The last day this pipeline saw the role on its board. The window column.

date_estimate.doc: Best available 'when did this role appear': posted_date if there is one, else first_seen.

date_basis.doc: Which date date_estimate came from, and how much to trust it.

enum.posted_date: the employer published a date and we use it
enum.first_seen: no published date; the day WE first saw it, which is an upper bound on how old the posting is
enum.first_seen_oldest_for_company: no published date, AND this is the oldest sighting we hold for this employer — so it may have arrived as part of a back catalogue when we started watching, rather than having been posted that day. Treat the date as 'not newer than this' only.

days_observed.doc: Days from the FIRST day we ever saw this role (across all its spells) to the last, inclusive. Days we observed it, not days it was open — we only see it when a scan runs.

closed_on.doc: The day we recorded it closed. Empty while open.

emailed.doc: true if this role went out in a daily digest email.

emailed_on.doc: The date it was first emailed. Empty if never emailed.

episodes.doc: How many separate spells we have seen this role open (a reappearance after an absence starts a new one).

reposts.doc: How many times the employer bumped posted_date 3+ days past the start of the current spell.

repost_dates.doc: The posted_date values those bumps landed on, separated by ';'.

sources.doc: Which fetchers saw it (greenhouse, comeet, scrape, ...), separated by ';'.

host.doc: The hostname of url — the ATS or careers domain the posting lives on.

seniority_title.doc: Seniority read from the TITLE ALONE by keyword. Not the years figure.

enum.senior: the title says senior/lead/principal/staff (or the Hebrew equivalent)
enum.junior: the title says junior/entry-level and does not also say senior
enum.unknown: the title carries no seniority word — most titles

years_experience.doc: Years of experience asked for, read from the DESCRIPTION text. Empty when the text does not say.

family.doc: Role family, from title first and the opening of the description second.

enum.Product Analyst: role family, read from the title first and the opening of the description second
enum.Marketing Analyst: role family, read from the title first and the opening of the description second
enum.BI & DWH: role family, read from the title first and the opening of the description second
enum.Data Engineering: role family, read from the title first and the opening of the description second
enum.Data Science: role family, read from the title first and the opening of the description second
enum.Product Manager: role family, read from the title first and the opening of the description second
enum.Business Analyst: role family, read from the title first and the opening of the description second
enum.Data Analyst: role family, read from the title first and the opening of the description second
enum.Other: an analytics role that fits none of the families above

track.doc: IC = individual contributor, Lead = the title names a lead/manager/head.

enum.Lead: the title names a lead, manager or head

degree_level.doc: Highest degree the posting requires or prefers.

degree_status.doc: Whether that degree is required or merely preferred.

degree_fields.doc: Fields of study named alongside it, separated by ';'.

enum.CS: field of study named alongside the degree
field of study named alongside the degree
enum.Info Systems: field of study named alongside the degree
enum.Statistics: field of study named alongside the degree
enum.Economics: field of study named alongside the degree
enum.Math: field of study named alongside the degree
enum.Engineering: field of study named alongside the degree
enum.Business: field of study named alongside the degree
enum.Finance: field of study named alongside the degree
enum.Life Sciences: field of study named alongside the degree

ai.doc: How the posting expects AI to be used, separated by ';'. Empty when AI is not mentioned.

enum.AI for efficiency: Expected to use AI tools (Copilot, ChatGPT, Cursor…) to work faster
enum.AI for automation: Using AI to automate processes and workflows
enum.Building with AI: Building AI/LLM-powered features, models or data products
enum.AI (unspecified): AI named as a requirement without a stated purpose

skills.doc: Every skill found in title+description, separated by ';', in extraction order.

class_decision.doc: The classifier's verdict on the role when it was last judged.

enum.accept: judged an analytics role in Israel

class_path.doc: How that verdict was reached: keyword, llm, llm_cache, ...

class_contract.doc: Which classifier contract (the hash of its rules and model, e.g. v3.0f84ab84) made that verdict. Equal to the meta's classifier_contract.live: judged under the rules that are live today. Different: judged under retired rules and not re-judged since -- a closed role never re-enters the run, so its verdict is frozen on the day it closed. Empty: not recorded, which is every cell stamped before 2026-09-11 and every verdict served from the cache without the seam saying which contract answered.

description_len.doc: Characters of description text we hold. 0 when we captured none.

description_truncated.doc: true when the text sits exactly on the 6,000-character capture cap, i.e. the real posting is longer.

description_sha1.doc: sha1 of the description text; join to roles_text.jsonl to read it.

description_quality.doc: Whether the text we hold reads as a job description (jdfill.looks_like_jd). Empty = text exists but could not be judged this run.

enum.jd: the stored text passes the same two tests a fresh fetch must (jdfill.looks_like_jd): >= 300 characters of body and >= 2 section families
enum.snippet: we hold text but it fails that test — a search snippet, page furniture or a fragment; description_len says how much; do not read it as the full posting (the test can also fail a genuinely terse real ad)
enum.none: this record holds no description text (description_len 0); a stale line may linger in roles_text.jsonl under the same role_id

description_blocker.doc: Why a weak text (description_quality snippet/none) is structurally hard to complete, or empty. Recorded verdicts (jd-text's matched.jd_why, 'structural:*') verbatim; else derived: 'gone' (the posting 404s on the employer's own board), 'unfillable:<why>' (a host no rung we own can read), 'listing-page' (the only address we hold is a shared listing, not the posting's own). Under the live policy (meta description_text.blocked.policy — 'exclude' since the operator's 2026-09-01 ruling) a blocked row is excluded from this file with its reason counted in the meta; a weak row with NO blocker is pending a fill and stays; the archive keeps history either way.

stage_note.doc: Ticker or acquisition note behind that stage.

business_model.doc: How the company earns money (firmographics, free text).

customer_type.doc: Who buys from it (firmographics, free text).

firmo_as_of.doc: The date those company facts were researched.

firmo_match.doc: How the company facts were matched to this row's company_registry (the brand in `company` renders only on an exact match).

enum.exact: company facts matched this row's company name exactly
enum.identity: matched after normalising the name (suffixes, aliases, 'X Israel')
enum.none: we hold no researched facts for this company; every firmographics column is empty
